name: spawn_room
caption: strangers keep spawning by my bed 😐
logline: Forty-one strangers have appeared next to a boy's bed; each walks outside and punches a tree, so the boy follows a compass to find where they come from, and it leads him home.
question: why tf do strangers keep appearing next to his bed?
premise: Strangers appear out of nowhere beside a boy's bed in the cottage he shares with his grandpa, a cartographer. They never talk; each walks outside and punches a tree, so every tree near the house floats. Some come back the same night with nothing; one came back a year later and left a cake. Every compass in the village points at his bed. Grandpa: 'Everybody starts somewhere.'
twist: His bedroom is world spawn. Every new player in the world starts next to his bed, respawns there after their first night's death, and punches the nearest tree. He follows a compass for three days and it brings him home to his bed, where a stranger appears on that exact block, and the chat fills with 'joined the game' as twelve more arrive at once.

N.name: me
N.profile: a boy of about twelve, deadpan and tired, telling something absurd as if it were the weather; dry, unhurried, easy-going; a crack of real unease only near the end
N.on_screen: pov (hand visible, holding the compass from L10); never seen

Grandpa.name: Grandpa
Grandpa.profile: his grandfather, an old cartographer; gravelly, slow, amused by everything, never looks up from his maps; calls everyone 'kid'
Grandpa.on_screen: villager, plains, cartographer (monocle), no name tag

requests.direction: A quiet cottage on a hill. A boy tells a strange story with a straight face, dry and tired; his grandfather answers slowly, gravelly and amused, as if none of it is strange.

lines.text: FORTY-ONE strangers / have appeared / next to my BED.
lines.say: Forty-one strangers... have appeared next to my bed.
lines.direction: deadpan and tired, like reporting the weather; a beat before the number

lines.text: They don't KNOCK. / They don't TALK. / They just APPEAR.
lines.direction: dry and unhurried; a tiny pause before the last word

lines.text: Then they walk / OUTSIDE, / and PUNCH / a TREE.
That's why / every tree / near our house / FLOATS.
lines.direction: resigned, matter-of-fact, as if it's obvious

lines.text: Some come back / the SAME night, / with NOTHING, / looking UPSET.
One came back / a YEAR later / and left me / a CAKE.
Leave 'em BE, kid. / Everybody starts / SOMEWHERE.
lines.say: Leave 'em be, kid. <short pause> Everybody starts somewhere.
lines.direction: gravelly and amused, not looking up; a smile on the last word

lines.text: And every COMPASS / in the village / points at my BED.

lines.direction: unbothered and fond, as if it's the most obvious thing in the world

lines.text: So I took / a COMPASS / and LEFT, / to find where / they come FROM.
lines.say: So... I took a compass and left, to find where they come from.
lines.direction: resolute; a held breath before he starts

lines.text: THREE days / of walking. / It kept pointing / BEHIND me.

lines.direction: almost a whisper; the last word lands in silence

beats: on 'BED', a stranger (Noor skin) appears on the exact block the needle points at, nose to nose with the camera; chat: 'Noor joined the game' (yellow)

S14 (no line, ~3.5 s): the room from the corner; eleven more appear one after another on the same spot, pushing each other off it; the chat scrolls 'Zuri joined the game', 'Efe joined the game', 'Kai joined the game'... (each line also in the caption track)
the crowd turns, files out of the door
S15 with L14: dawn, the hilltop, twelve strangers spread into the woods and each punches a tree; tree after tree is left floating
ending.loop: the last image (strangers punching the last trees) runs into L01's first frame, a stranger by the bed

shots.camera: pov from the doorway, slow push in
shots.frame: fg: the door frame and the carpet runner; subject: a stranger (Kai skin) standing beside the bed, arms down, slowly turning his head; bg: the bed, the window with the moonlit floating trees, a lantern. Night.

shots.camera: pov, a step closer, then a small turn toward the bed on 'APPEAR'
shots.frame: subject: Kai, waist up, looking at his empty hands, then at us; on 'APPEAR' a second stranger (Alex skin) pops into being on the bedside block behind him

shots.camera: pov from the cottage door, looking out; Alex walks left to right
shots.frame: fg: the doorstep; subject: Alex walking out and punching the nearest oak, the bottom log cracking and breaking; bg: more trees, already floating, and the valley. Dawn.

shots.camera: at: 40 blocks out over the slope, slow push toward the cottage
shots.frame: fg: a floating oak, its canopy and two logs hovering 2 blocks over grass; mid: the cottage on the hilltop in a ring of 40+ floating trees; bg: the village in the valley, the river, the mountains. Morning.

shots.camera: pov from the bed's foot, still
shots.frame: subject: Kai again, head to foot by the bed, empty-handed, spinning round to face the door; bg: through the window, a zombie standing in the dark under the floating trees. Night.

shots.camera: pov from the doorway (as S01, by day)
shots.frame: fg: the door frame; subject: a cake on the floor beside the bed, a stranger (Steve skin) walking out of frame right past the camera; bg: the window, the trees, daylight
fg: the table edge, a map and an empty cartography table; subject: Grandpa, waist up, eyes on his work, not looking up; bg: shelves, a lantern, the window. Evening.

shots.camera: pov walking up to Grandpa's market stall in the village
shots.frame: fg: the stall's counter; subject: a wall of 8 item frames, each holding a compass, every needle tilted the same way; bg: past the stall's corner, up the hill, the cottage and its floating trees (the needles point at it). Day.

shots.camera: pov, turning from the compass wall to Grandpa behind the counter
shots.frame: subject: Grandpa, waist up, unrolling a map, not looking up; bg: the compass wall at frame left

shots.camera: pov leaving the cottage door, the compass in hand
shots.frame: fg: the hand holding a compass; mid: the path down the hill between floating trees; bg: the valley and the far mountains. Dawn.

shots.camera: pov on a ridge, looking out, then a glance down at the compass
shots.frame: fg: the compass in hand, its needle pointing back over his shoulder (toward the bottom of the frame); mid: the ridge falling away; bg: a different land: mountains, a river, another valley in fog. Dusk, day three.

shots.camera: pov from the foot of the hill, walking up the path
shots.frame: fg: the compass in hand pointing straight ahead; mid: the path; bg: the cottage on the hill, one lit window, floating trees silhouetted against the moon. Night.

shots.camera: pov from the doorway stepping to the bed, compass held out
shots.frame: fg: the compass, needle pointing at the bedside block; subject: the empty block beside the bed; on 'BED' Noor appears on it, face to face with us; chat line 'Noor joined the game'

shots.camera: at: high in the corner opposite the door, looking down at the bed
shots.frame: the whole room: the boy small by the door (back to us), the bed, eleven strangers appearing one after another on the bedside block and shoving each other off it; the chat scrolling 'joined the game' lines; then they all turn to the door

shots.camera: at: as S04 but from the other side, dawn
shots.frame: fg: a whole oak about to float; mid: twelve strangers spreading out over the hilltop, each to a tree, punching; bg: the cottage, the valley, the sunrise
